doc.title: Hentoff Nat — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Overlooked Boston players; setting up Mingus for tomorrow
summary: He names lesser-known Boston players like Joe Gordon and Sabby Lewis; Schoenberg defers Mingus, whom Hentoff met in Boston.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Before we leave Boston – we already left, but before we leave Boston, you mentioned that dixieland scene and some of these musicians. Can you give us the names of musicians unlike the ones that we just talked about, Ruby and Vic and Sid Catlett – the ones who didn’t leave Boston or the ones you heard that impressed you, who have fallen into obscurity, because they either never recorded or never played too much?

Among the dixieland players, there was this trombonist, Ralph Firino. There was a pianist named Ed Swartz. John Field sat in with everybody. At the Savoy, Sabby Lewis had the house band. He was good, but he had a trumpet player who should have been much better known, Joe Gordon. He had a tenor saxophonist who became very well known, Paul Quinichette – Paul Gonsalves, rather. The local scene, there were some very, very good musicians. Sandy Sanderford was a pianist and arranger. I expect – I had left by the time Herb Pomeroy had become the center of another jazz scene. But you have that in every city I hear about. This band I heard about in Honolulu and did the liner notes for. Lord knows what we have going on around the country.

So you’re in New York and you’re the editor – you’ve mentioned his name already, and I’m wondering when – actually I think, if you don’t mind, I’m going to wait until tomorrow to really get into Charles Mingus, because that’s going to be a long one.
Yeah, I met him in Boston.

Oh, actually you met him in Boston? Why don’t we kick off tomorrow – I’m just going to make a note that when we come back tomorrow, I’m going to start with Mingus, because I don’t want there to be any limit on that in terms of time.
